title: add RAG agent quickstart + TypeScript tool-calling example
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers frequently ask for a concise, runnable example that demonstrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) wired to an agent that can call tools (search, vector DB query, and an external action API). This PR adds a self-contained quickstart that lives in examples/rag-agent-ts and a complementary docs site page under redwood-docs/content/quickstarts. Motivation: reduce time-to-first-success for engineers evaluating RAG+agent patterns and provide a TypeScript-first sample that mirrors our SDK conventions and streaming/tool-calling behavior. Changes: - New example folder: examples/rag-agent-ts with README.md, sample code (agent.ts), a simple in-memory vector DB adapter (vector_adapter.ts), and mocks for a search tool and an external action tool. - Docs page: docs/content/quickstarts/rag-agent-quickstart.md with step-by-step instructions, configuration flags (warming cache, batching hints), and troubleshooting. - Tests: a lightweight integration test under examples/rag-agent-ts/test/integration.test.ts that runs the agent against mocked tools and asserts the call sequence. - CI: updated examples CI job to build and run the example test and to render a docs preview. - Minor SDK compat shim: a 12-line helper in examples that demonstrates the current SDK streaming API and function-calling contract (kept forward-compatible). Checklist: - [x] Example code compiles and runs locally - [x] Integration test added and green in CI - [x] Docs page added and renders in docs preview - [x] Reviewers addressed comments - [x] Changelog/release notes included Usage notes: The README contains exact commands (npm i, npm run start -- --local-index) and a single-command demo that spins up a lightweight local index and runs the sample prompt flow. Security: example uses mocked credentials and an in-memory index; production notes explicitly call out KMS/HSM and VPC recommendations. Backwards compatibility: no changes to public SDK interfaces; the tiny compatibility shim is isolated under examples/ and marked experimental. Related: this PR complements the eval-harness RAG prompt sets (ENG-3892) and the private deployment docs where examples are referenced.
